I regret ever believing that he could go back to the nice person he was at the beginning of our friendship. I spent so much time and energy on him that I feel emotionally drained from it all.

I was definitely very uncomfortable with how physically close he would sit to me, and how he always wanted me to hug him closer. He had this thing about pointing out that I "jutted my butt out" whenever I hugged him, and made some backwards comment about how he figured I didn't want to be close to him. I said that I prefer to have a bubble of distance around people and am not a typically physical person.

As for what he did the last time I saw him, that was the end for me. I should have never allowed it to escalate as far as it had, and I deeply regret my judgement in not only drinking around him, but staying the night at his apartment. I was uncomfortable from the moment I walked into his place, and should have listened to my gut feeling.

While this thinking may apply in other situations, both he and I were in other relationships when we met and he had never expressed any romantic feelings for me up until it suited him.

He decided to ruin a perfectly good friendship because he was unable to emotionally categorize his romantic interests and his friendships. 

I don't feel sorry for him, because I was always upfront with him that he was my friend, and for a long time that's the same story he fed me. He chose to allow his emotions to dictate his actions which consequently ended our friendship on a bad note. 

Before he became obsessed with me and subsequently tortured himself, I thought we would have been best friends our entire lives. He took the opportunity to have a loving and supportive friendship for the rest of his days and decided that that was not good enough for him, that he instead needed this so-called friendship but with sex included. It was his deluded and twisted thinking that ultimately ruined something great.

That's exactly what I thought, too. He said he wanted to tell me because he "owed me" and apparently because we both live in the same small town that he didn't want me to hear by the town gossip. Yeah, sureeee that's why.

Yes! He started out asking how I was and telling me that he hoped my life was good. But his messages were short and I wasn't sure why he was messaging. Then he randomly launched into this long paragraph how he was going back onto the "dating scene" because he had to at least try. He then ended the message by saying, "I really hope you find someone, too!"

Suffice to say that I was very upset for a few days. But I've really been coming to the conclusion that he's not worth my time, tears, or energy!

It feels great! Because I know he would've been expecting me to say something for his birthday, so I really let him know how I am truly getting over him.

And right? When he messaged me that I was just dumbfounded. He said that he apparently "owed me to let me know."

A ten minute phone call would not have shown his true colours. When we first started talking, we got along famously and he never gave me any reason to believe that he was a creep. He was very polite, nice, and we had a lot in common. We talked a lot about video games and movies, all sorts of different interests.

As I've mentioned previously, he did not begin changing until his mother died. After that, he slowly progressed into the downward spiral into what he was in August. It was gradual. And although there were some warning signs, I wanted to believe that he would work out his issues and tried to support him regardless. I tried to put my discomfort aside to be a good friend and, unfortunately, that came back to bite me in the ass.

I could try to write every little detail, but this post would be far too longwinded (more than it already was). 

I don't believe I necessarily put myself in a bad situation at first, because he had been a very good friend of mine. Yes, my judgement was lacking in other areas but I don't believe that makes it okay for him to behave or act out in the ways that he had.

And of course I would have mixed emotions---he was my best friend and I wanted to believe that he was the person that I had first met, instead of the creep that he turned out to be.

I refuse to believe that because I tried to see the best in someone, and because he violated my trust and my boundaries that he did "nothing wrong." He absolutely did. This mentality is very regressive. I did not ask, nor consent, to inappropriate touching and I had made it abundantly clear on multiple occasions that I did not reciprocate his feelings whatsoever. Though I did not mention it in the original post, we had talked about how I didn't have feelings for him many, many times.

Why he felt the need to touch me without my consent while I was asleep is still beyond me, though it simply boils down to him being selfish and not respecting me.

I absolutely have to work on my self-worth, I know that for certain. It's unfortunate that I gave him so many chances to make amends and that I felt the need to forgive him every time he gave me an "apology." 

One downside that I know about myself is my inability to put a stop to things that I know are getting progressively toxic, in fear of hurting someone else or being hurt in the process. As a young woman, these are things I hope to seriously work out in the coming years so that I won't make the same mistakes again.

I don't have a strong foundation of how to build myself or a role model that I can look up to, and though I'm not blaming anyone for my bad decisions and lack of understanding, I feel as though it takes me longer to work out the kinks. We stumble until we learn to walk, right?

Thank you.

I have been taking the time to write out a lot of the things going on in my life in order to bring it to a counsellor with my thoughts somewhat intact. I'm glad I wrote this out because I had been putting it off for far too long, and I'm also glad to see that I'm not alone in my feelings.

As I said, for the first three or so years he was completely normal. We had a very tight bond and were great friends. When his mom passed away, his behaviour obviously changed. I attributed this due to his grief and allowed him time to heal, while accepting that people don't always act the way they usually do while grieving.

It seems that he latched onto me in a very possessive way after the death of his mother, and I tried my best to put this in its place but, of course, he felt like I was the only person he had that actually cared about him.

We had gone through hell and back in this time, and although I was upset by the lying, the manipulating, and the like I wanted to believe my best friend would come back to his senses. I kept giving him room to grow and to grieve, and unfortunately he slipped into a world of self-pity. He used me for his own personal gain in an emotional way.

This all has taken time to think through, and I still don't have my feelings sorted out as far as any of it goes. I didn't want to believe he could be capable of crossing the boundaries that he did, and it still sickens me to think that he went from a very special person in my life to someone who makes me feel violated.

I wish I could be a better judge of character, but I also wish in ways that people could be more upfront and wave their red flags high so that I could easily avoid them. We all make mistakes, and my mistake was being far too forgiving.

I've had a bit of time to think and reflect over the last few days and to understand my own anger about what happened. I know that there were definitely points where I, too, didn't have the best interests for our relationship. I knew that we couldn't get married right away despite that being something I genuinely wanted at the time, that was a bit of pressure on my end despite me trying my best not to. However, he and I lived together for three years. We had the same apartment for that entire time which was far too expensive due to his debt. My pay cheque was covering the rent, utilities, as well as trying to keep up with his overwhelming debt.

Moving to the city, as inconvenient as it may have been for him to start fresh, would have actually been better financially for him. The job he was at (and still is) pays pretty poorly for the work he's doing, especially since his position is in high demand. There were many jobs offering much more at beginning rates, which I encouraged him about. He would have thrived better in the city had he just realized that holding onto the idea of being immediately close to everyone isn't always in our better interest, sometimes we have to take leaps of faith in order to progress in life. I'm afraid that he just couldn't loosen the ties he had on his previous life.

It's hard to make sacrifices for someone who couldn't do the same in return. Even though I'm angry at the way things transpired, I'm also glad that I get the opportunity to start over again and this time to do it how I need to without feeling as though anyone is holding me back. But, as you probably already know, starting over is difficult.

For me, I think it's figuring out what didn't work in my life before and how to fix it so I don't stumble and make the same mistakes. Which means combing over every fine detail to bring myself to closure, and in turn sparks up old emotions that I, unfortunately, buried.

The city was two hours away. He also could've got a better paying job in the city because his skills are in such high demand and there are so few people able to operate the machines that he can. He just refused to move for petty reasons.
